name: Produce monthly client reports
summary: Each month the client reporting team builds a report for each of five client portfolios showing market values by pool and asset class, units held, returns against benchmarks, asset mix against policy ranges, cash flows, rebalancing and compliance with the client's investment policy. The work cannot finish until fund accounting signs off the month-end books and the performance team releases approved returns, so most of the elapsed time is waiting. Analysts then reconcile figures across accounting, performance, private markets and risk sources in spreadsheets, a second analyst and the manager review, and the relationship manager releases it. Late private market values, restated returns and manual workbook assembly are the usual causes of delay and error.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial not-for-profit asset manager running pooled funds and segregated accounts for four public-sector clients with five portfolios, with a small client reporting team that assembles tailored reports from a data warehouse and spreadsheets.
baseline.notes: Snapshot of 2021 with five client portfolios; in 2019 there were three. Report format is one core suite tailored per client (mgr_ar20).

trigger: Month end: the reporting cycle opens on the first business day; work proceeds as the signed-off accounting package and approved performance results arrive.
end_state: The approved report is delivered to the client's authorised contacts and the delivery is logged against the service level, or a corrected version is reissued.

volume.seasonality: One report per client portfolio every month. December reports take longer because of year-end adjustments; the month after quarter-end private valuations are approved carries restatement bridges.

evidence.note: Five client portfolios in 2021 per the organisation file (The pension client, the insurance client insurance fund and loss of retirement income fund, judges' plan, WISE Trust); clients' agreements set reporting frequency (pclient_ar21). Monthly frequency is common practice (cutter_freq) but the model manager's exact monthly content is not published.

Cost from the organisation file, built on Job Bank Toronto wages for NOC 11101 (jobbank_11101). Tasks follow a client reporting analyst posting (ca_job). Three analysts also handle cash instructions, service requests and quarterly reports.
Cost from the organisation file on Job Bank NOC 10010 (jobbank_10010); share of time is an author estimate.

Organisation file cost on NOC 11101 wages; time answering report queries is an author estimate.

Pool unitholder register and transfer agency records (custodian module with controlled spreadsheets)
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Document management system and virtual data rooms

steps.name: Open the monthly cycle and roll forward report templates
steps.description: On the first business day after month end the analyst copies last month's report workbook and presentation shell for the client portfolio, updates dates and period labels, checks the client's current policy asset mix and ranges against the latest investment policy, and refreshes the reporting calendar tracker.

error.defect_description: Policy weights or ranges not updated after a client policy change.

evidence.note: Author estimate of template preparation at an institutional manager producing one tailored monthly package per client portfolio; the model manager introduced a standard core report suite in 2020 (mgr_ar20) but each client portfolio has its own mix.

steps.name: Wait for signed-off month-end accounting package
steps.description: The analyst watches the close tracker and the fund accounting mailbox until the pools and the client's segregated accounts are signed off for the month. Nothing in the report can be finalised before accounting values and unit balances are approved, so the case waits on the fund accounting close.
outputs: confirmation that the NAV package is final

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Public pension custody standards set month-end close targets of business day 5 for external accounts, 10 for internal and commingled funds and 15 for alternatives (nmerb_ps); a pool and segregated-account close around business day 6 to 9 is assumed, which is 8 to 12 calendar days.

steps.name: Extract holdings, market values and units
steps.description: The analyst runs the warehouse reports for the client portfolio: market value by pool and segregated strategy, units held in each pool from the unitholder register, accrued income and cash. The output is pasted into the report workbook, which still holds several manual mapping tabs.

error.defect_description: Wrong extract date or mapping of a new account to the wrong asset class.

evidence.note: Data input and exhibit building are core client reporting tasks (ca_job); 49% of firms still rely mainly on manual processing (cutter_cr2020). Touch time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Load private holdings values and commitments
steps.description: The analyst pulls the latest approved values, unfunded commitments, and the month's capital calls and distributions for the client's private market holdings from the private markets system. Most values are the last quarter-end valuation rolled forward for cash flows, which the report must footnote.

error.defect_description: A call or distribution booked in the wrong month or to the wrong client account.

next.condition: values or cash flows missing for some holdings

evidence.note: Private equity values typically lag one calendar quarter and are adjusted for cash flows (prim_rfp); the insurance client requires non-traded values at least annually, reviewed quarterly (iclient_if). Share of months with missing items is an author estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing private market values or cash flows
steps.description: The analyst emails private markets operations and valuations with the list of holdings whose value or latest cash flow is missing or does not match the prior report, and waits for the corrected booking or a confirmation that the prior value stands.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Late private market values are named in the process map as a usual cause of delay; the wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile values and units to the accounting package
steps.description: The analyst ties the report's market values by pool and account to the signed-off NAV package and the units to the unitholder register, and checks that opening values equal last month's closing values. Differences above the tolerance are listed for fund accounting.

error.defect_description: A real break is cleared as a timing difference.

control.basis: The model manager SOC 1 report (CSAE 3416 / SSAE 18 examination): reconciliation and client reporting control objectives that statements show the correct holdings and market value

evidence.note: Baseline SOC 1 objective for client statements (sifma_soc1); the model manager obtained a SOC 1 Type I in 2021 (mgr_ar21); reconciling all client data before report generation (ca_job). Break rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Resolve break with fund accounting
steps.description: A fund accountant investigates each listed difference, usually an accrual, a late trade, a private market booking or a unit transaction dated in the wrong period, and either corrects the books or explains it. The analyst then re-runs the reconciliation.

error.defect_description: Correction posted to the wrong account.

evidence.note: Author estimate; fund accountants also work the close for nine pools and portfolios.

steps.name: Load approved returns and check returns, mix and ranges
steps.description: When the performance team releases approved returns, the analyst loads portfolio, asset class and benchmark returns for the month, quarter to date, year to date and longer periods, then checks that the asset mix sits within the client's policy ranges and that total fund return agrees with the sum of its parts.

error.defect_description: Benchmark return for a long period copied from the wrong column.

evidence.note: Preliminary monthly performance is due about ten business days after month end at a public pension custodian (ocers_qa); the model manager returns are net of costs and time-weighted (mgr_ar22). Wait and query rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Explain or correct the return difference
steps.description: A performance analyst checks the queried return or benchmark, typically a late private market cash flow, a cost accrual, a blended benchmark weight or a restated prior month, and either confirms the figure with an explanation or issues a corrected result.

error.defect_description: Corrected figure not propagated to all periods.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Add cash flows, unit transactions and rebalancing
steps.description: The analyst adds the month's client contributions and withdrawals, the pool units issued and redeemed with prices, and the rebalancing switches and overlay changes made by total portfolio management, taken from the register and the rebalancing log.

error.defect_description: A switch shown as an external cash flow.

evidence.note: Content follows the process map description of the monthly package; time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Add risk summary and policy compliance section
steps.description: The analyst inserts the risk team's monthly figures for the portfolio and the list of confirmed guideline or policy breaches with remediation from the compliance exception log, and drafts the compliance statement for the month.

error.defect_description: A breach closed in the month left out of the statement.

evidence.note: The insurance client reviews performance, risk and compliance at least quarterly and liquidity monthly (iclient_if); wait for the risk report is an author estimate.

steps.name: Confirm the policy compliance statement
steps.description: A compliance analyst compares the draft statement with the compliance engine's breach log and open cases for the client's accounts and pools and confirms or corrects the wording before the report goes further.

error.defect_description: An open case is not mentioned.

control.basis: Client investment management agreement and statement of investment policies: The model manager reports compliance with the client's policies and restrictions

evidence.note: Compliance reporting is part of the client's oversight (iclient_if) and the reporting content is set in the client's service level agreement (pclient_ar21). Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Check for restated prior months
steps.description: The analyst reads the performance team's release note to see whether new quarter-end private valuations restated earlier months. If so the report needs a bridge from the previously reported figures to the restated ones.

error.defect_description: Restatement not noticed.

evidence.note: Estimated private values are adjusted when final values arrive (gips_ao 22.A.18); fund reports arrive about 60 days after quarter end (ilpa_faq), so roughly one month in three carries restatements. Share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Prepare restatement bridge and footnote
steps.description: The analyst builds a table showing each affected month as first reported and as restated, with the cause, and writes a footnote. The bridge is checked against the performance team's restatement memo.

error.defect_description: Bridge uses a superseded prior figure.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Draft performance and market commentary
steps.description: The analyst writes a page of commentary on the month: market moves, the portfolio's return against its benchmark by asset class, main contributors from the attribution, and any rebalancing or policy breaches, reusing house market views where available.

error.defect_description: Commentary cites a number that differs from the tables.

evidence.note: The model manager provides market updates, performance recaps and commentary tailored to each client (mgr_ar20); time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Assemble the package and complete the checklist
steps.description: The analyst assembles tables, charts, commentary and footnotes into the client's format, then works the reporting checklist: totals foot, opening equals prior closing, periods and labels correct, every table ties to the reconciliation sheet.

error.defect_description: Chart not refreshed after a late correction.

evidence.note: Exhibits and quality control are standard analyst duties (ca_job). Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Peer check by a second analyst
steps.description: Another client reporting analyst re-performs a sample of tie-outs, reads every table against the reconciliation sheet and the performance release, and marks errors on the draft for the preparer to fix.

error.defect_description: Error missed by the reviewer.

control.basis: Maker-checker review of client reports before distribution under the client reporting procedures

next.condition: no errors or minor fixes made

evidence.note: Review of client statements before release supports the SOC 1 client reporting objective (sifma_soc1); error rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Manager reviews and signs off
steps.description: The manager of client reporting reads the report, focusing on commentary, unusual movements, restatements and the compliance statement, compares headline figures with the other client portfolios for consistency and signs the checklist.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: The model manager SOC 1 client reporting control: documented management review of client reports before distribution

evidence.note: SOC 1 Type 2 coverage of the model manager controls from October 2021 (mgr_ar22); baseline client reporting objective (sifma_soc1). Rework share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Relationship manager approves release
steps.description: The client relationship manager reads the summary and commentary for messages the client may react to, such as underperformance, a breach or a restatement, and either approves release or asks for wording changes and prepares to call the client.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Release by the relationship manager is stated in the process map; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Finalise PDF and verify the distribution list
steps.description: The analyst converts the approved files to a locked PDF, applies the version and confidentiality marking, and checks the recipient list against the client's authorised contacts recorded in the CRM before sending.

error.defect_description: Report addressed to a former client contact.

control.basis: The model manager confidentiality and information handling policy: client information sent only to authorised recipients

evidence.note: Common practice; author estimate.

steps.name: Send the report and log delivery
steps.description: The analyst sends the PDF and data file to the client through secure email or file transfer, records the delivery date against the service level in the CRM and files the final version with the checklist and reconciliation as evidence.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Client service level agreement: content and timing of monthly reporting

next.condition: error found after release by the client or internally

evidence.note: A service level agreement sets the content and frequency of the model manager's reporting (pclient_ar21); post-release error share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Correct and reissue the report
steps.description: When the client or a later process finds an error in a released report, the analyst corrects the affected tables, adds a note explaining the change and logs the error, and the corrected report goes back through manager sign-off.

error.defect_description: Correction introduces a new inconsistency.

control.basis: Report error correction procedure: corrected reports reissued to every recipient of the erroneous report

evidence.note: Corrected reports go to the oversight body that received the erroneous one (gips_ao 21.A.16); firms keep error logs and review errors in committees (cfa_errors). Times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Accounting break at reconciliation
exceptions.description: Report values or units do not agree with the signed-off accounting package; fund accounting explains or corrects before the report can continue.

exceptions.name: Missing private market values or cash flows
exceptions.description: Some private holdings lack a current value or a booked call or distribution, so the analyst chases private markets operations.

exceptions.name: Restated prior months
exceptions.description: Quarter-end private valuations approved this month restate earlier returns, and the report adds a bridge from reported to restated figures.

exceptions.name: Return query to performance
exceptions.description: A return, benchmark or total does not tie, and the performance team explains or corrects it.

exceptions.name: Reissue after post-release error
exceptions.description: An error is found after delivery; the report is corrected, re-signed and reissued to all recipients.

exceptions.name: Warehouse load failure
exceptions.description: The overnight warehouse load fails or is incomplete on extract day, and the analyst waits for data engineering to rerun it before extracting again.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to delivery of the monthly client report
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a multi-client public asset manager, anchored on public pension custody service levels

evidence.note: Preliminary performance is due about 10 business days after month end and final before the next month end (ocers_qa); custody close targets run to business day 15 for alternatives (nmerb_ps). A client report a week after approved performance gives about business day 14 to 15, or 20 calendar days; p90 allows for private value chases and restatements.

benchmarks.population: Custody services RFP of a US county public pension system, 2022
Custody bank performance standards of a US state educational retirement board, 2024
Cutter Associates 2020 Client Reporting Benchmarking Survey as reported in 2021

evidence.note: About one-third monthly and two-thirds quarterly.

benchmarks.population: Cutter Associates 2020 Client Reporting Benchmarking Survey (firms with over USD 16 trillion AUM)

pain_points.description: The report cannot be finished until accounting and performance sign off, so the team has idle days followed by a crunch, and any upstream delay passes straight to the client.

evidence.note: Upstream close and performance deadlines from public pension custody service levels.

pain_points.description: Assembly in spreadsheets with manual mapping and copy-paste between warehouse extracts, performance output and the client's format causes errors and repeated tie-outs.

evidence.note: 49% of firms rely mainly on manual processing and lack of automation is the top challenge for 63%.

pain_points.description: Private market values lag by a quarter and are restated when final values arrive, so reports carry footnotes and bridges that clients query.

evidence.note: Lagged private values and adjustment when final values arrive.

pain_points.description: Data quality problems surface late in the cycle as reconciliation breaks between warehouse, accounting and performance figures.

evidence.note: Only 5% of firms say their data is consistently high quality.

assumptions: Volume is five client portfolio reports a month (the 2021 state in the organisation file); the low of three reflects 2019.

The case starts at month end, so the cycle time includes waiting for the fund accounting close and performance release; these waits are modelled as wait_before_min on s02 and s08 rather than as separate upstream steps.
Interface shares for triggered_by give the share of months in which each input is usually the last to arrive and so releases the work; every report uses all six inputs.

The model manager's monthly report content, service levels and review chain are not published. Content follows the process map; the maker-checker, manager sign-off and relationship manager release are typical practice and consistent with the model manager's SOC 1 reports from 2021 (mgr_ar21, mgr_ar22).
The compliance analyst and fund accountant are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process; they appear for short checks and break resolution.
Loaded hourly costs are taken unchanged from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus variable pay, times 1.35).

Stated FTE (1.15) is above the hands-on time implied by five reports a month because analysts also produce ad hoc client data cuts at month end and maintain templates and the reporting calendar, which are not modelled as steps.

Rework shares (20% reconciliation breaks, 16% return queries, 14% peer review returns, 15% manager changes, 4% post-release reissue) are author estimates for a spreadsheet-based process in 2019 to 2022.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: New client reporting suite in 2020 with a core set of concise reports for all clients; quarterly performance recaps, positioning and commentary; KPI framework; a consistent core team for client management teams and investment committees; cost allocation policy and guidelines for fair, consistent allocation to the model manager products, segregated assets and clients, overseen by a Cost Allocation Committee; tiered approval authorities; costs reported regularly to senior management, the Finance and Audit Committee and clients; returns net of all costs, time-weighted, based on daily calculations; total benchmark daily weighted by clients' investment in each strategy; 2020 total costs $384.3 million (55.3 cents per $100).

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Clean SOC 1 Type I report on the design of controls as at 30 September 2021, with Type II planned for 2022; Board and client reporting redesigned in 2021 including a Quarterly Risk Insights report; full cost recovery without profit; the model manager allocates to and recovers all operational costs from clients based on agreed cost allocation principles; 2021 total costs $473.7 million (63.1 cents per $100 of AUM), investment management costs $317.2 million, operating expenses $156.5 million; recovery of costs revenue $216.6 million; year-end receivable from clients for cost recoveries $36.6 million plus HST (2020: $17.7 million); external fees paid as agent and collected from clients; amounts collected in advance held as deferred recovery of costs; financial statements authorised by the Board on 24 February 2022; CEM benchmarking of costs.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: Inaugural SOC 1 Type 2 report with a clean opinion that controls were designed and operated effectively from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022; returns net of all costs using the time-weighted rate of return; benchmark policy under which Risk researches and reviews benchmarks, the Management Investment Committee recommends them and the Board approves them; net value added defined against the IPS benchmark; interim private markets administration software and a new risk and total portfolio system implemented in 2022.

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: The model manager manages Plan assets for a fee based on cost recovery and regularly reports on investment performance and risk to the pension client; an Investment Management Agreement, a Service Level Agreement setting the content and frequency of reporting and service levels, and an Implementation and Support Agreement covering budgeting and cost management; the pension client monitoring program; the model manager management fees of $97.7 million in 2021 representing the pension client's share of the model manager operating expenses charged back on a cost recovery basis, with external fees paid by the model manager on the pension client's behalf and reimbursed; the model manager costs 41 basis points against a target of 50 or lower; the Board and its committees met 37 times in 2021.

sources.title: Insurance fund (The insurance client web page with the statement of investment policies)
sources.supports: The model manager is sole investment manager; fund performance, risk and compliance are reviewed at least quarterly and the model manager's performance annually; liquidity monitored at least monthly; fair value estimates for non-traded investments made at least annually and reviewed at least quarterly, with third-party valuations checked for reasonableness by the model manager; the model manager establishes strategy benchmarks and must advise the insurance client of total fund benchmark changes.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Baseline asset manager SOC 1 scope including reconciliation and client reporting; baseline control objective that account statements reflect the correct holdings and market value and are provided to clients in a complete and timely manner; reconciliation objective that discrepancies are researched and resolved timely; account performance listed as not baseline and fee calculation and billing as another area to consider; IT general controls over job scheduling, logical access and change management.

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Time-weighted returns required for total funds; valuation at least monthly, at month end and on large cash flows; monthly returns geometrically linked; private market investments valued and returns calculated at least quarterly; when preliminary or estimated values are used the difference to the final value must be assessed and adjusted when the final value arrives (22.A.18); net-of-fees returns deduct transaction costs, external fees and investment management costs (22.A.24); material errors must be corrected and corrected reports given to the oversight body (21.A.16); benchmarks must reflect the mandate; reports to oversight bodies updated within 12 months of each annual period end.

sources.title: Cutter Associates releases 2020 Client Reporting Benchmarking Survey (news release)
sources.supports: Survey of firms with over USD 16 trillion AUM: 49% typically rely on manual processing; 15% have fully automated structured data collection; 30% of custom reporting is purely manual; lack of automation is the top challenge (63%) followed by customisation requests (61%); 5% say their data is consistently high quality and 56% typically high quality; 71% have a dedicated client reporting tool; 32% publish reports through a portal.

sources.title: How often should asset managers share data with clients?
sources.supports: Monthly reporting to institutional clients is still commonplace; Cutter's 2020 survey found about two-thirds of firms report to clients quarterly and about one-third monthly; daily data can contain cancelled trades, unresolved corporate actions and bad prices.

sources.title: How do firms treat errors in investment performance?
sources.supports: Survey of 146 GIPS-compliant firms: most use a two-part materiality test with absolute thresholds of 11 to 50 basis points and relative thresholds of 5% to 10%; 78% keep an Excel error-correction log; 59% have a formal committee that reviews errors; errors occur even with tight controls.

sources.title: Request for Proposals: Investment Performance Reporting Services
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Pension Reserves Investment Management Board (PRIM)
sources.supports: Scope for a public pension investment manager's performance reporting: monthly and quarterly packages from the custodian performance book of record; gross and net of fee returns at account, asset class and total fund level; benchmark comparison; attribution at total fund, asset class, sub asset class, manager and security level; custom benchmarks and composites. Sample report notes: private equity returns use the latest partnership valuations, typically lagging one calendar quarter, adjusted for cash flows; property and timber benchmarks lagged one quarter because they are published 25 days after quarter end.

sources.title: Custody Services RFP: Questions and Answers (October 2022)
sources.supports: Preliminary monthly performance report covering benchmark, portfolio and composite performance required no later than ten business days after month end; finalized performance report must be issued before the next month end.

sources.title: Custody Bank RFP, Appendix F: Performance Standards and Related Key Performance Indicators
sources.supports: Month-end close targets: 5th business day for externally managed and cash accounts, 10th for internally managed and commingled funds, 15th for alternative investment accounts; external manager position reconciliations typically received on business days 3 to 5; variances above 10 basis points of NAV explained; performance reporting due 5 business days after the month-end close; a performance revision above 5 basis points from custodian error counts as a failure; asset servicing invoices within 60 days of period end.

sources.title: Analyst, Client Reporting (job posting)
sources.publisher: Cambridge Associates via Built In Boston
sources.supports: Produce monthly and quarterly performance reports across asset classes including data input, reconciliation, exhibits and quality control; reconcile all underlying investment data for each client before report generation (total portfolio reconciliation); investigate data gaps and discrepancies; coordinate with operations on transactions, data readiness and benchmark updates; base pay USD 63,700 to 82,800.

sources.title: ILPA Reporting Template and ILPA Performance Templates: Frequently Asked Questions (January 2025)
sources.supports: Suggested delivery timeline, deferring to fund documents: direct funds 60 days after quarter end and 120 days after fiscal year end; funds of funds 120 and 180 days.
